pharm: Polymyxin E (colistin) cationic polypeptide antibiotic; oral/topical salt form, minimally absorbed from the gut
tags: Not FDA-approved (oral colistin sulphate not marketed in the US)
quick: Bowel/GI: 1.5-3 million units three times daily (oral)
Oral: minimal absorption, little systemic effect; caution
GI symptoms; neuro/renal signs only if systemic exposure suspected
summary: Colistin sulphate is the oral and topical salt form of colistin (polymyxin E), a cationic polypeptide antibiotic active against most aerobic Gram-negative bacteria. Given orally it is very poorly absorbed from the gastrointestinal tract, so it is used for bowel sterilization/decontamination and gut infections caused by susceptible Gram-negative organisms rather than for systemic infection. It is distinct from colistimethate sodium, the inactive prodrug given parenterally or by inhalation for systemic and respiratory infections, where nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity are the main concerns. Oral colistin sulphate is not approved by the US FDA.
indications: Bowel sterilization / gut decontamination of susceptible Gram-negative bacteria (e.g., pre-operative, selective digestive decontamination)
Gastrointestinal infections caused by susceptible Gram-negative organisms
Topical use for susceptible Gram-negative skin/ear infections (formulation-dependent)

dosage.d: 1.5 to 3 million units three times daily
dosage.n: Minimal systemic absorption; dose per local product (units vary by formulation)

dosage.d: 0.75 to 1.5 million units three times daily
0.25 to 0.5 million units three times daily
Often 4 x 1 million units daily (up to 4 x 2 million units daily)
dosage.n: Regimen and duration set by local infection-control protocol

dosage.d: Apply per product strength (often in combination preparations)
dosage.n: Local use only; follow specific product instructions

admin: Administer orally; may be given with or without food
Oral colistin sulphate is for local gut effect - it is poorly absorbed and not used for systemic infection
Do not substitute for colistimethate sodium when systemic or inhaled therapy is intended
Reconstitute oral suspensions per product instructions and use within the stated period
Reserve systemic polymyxins (colistimethate) as last-resort agents for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections under specialist guidance
moa: Colistin (polymyxin E) is a cationic cyclic polypeptide that binds the anionic lipopolysaccharide of the Gram-negative outer membrane, displacing calcium and magnesium bridges and disrupting membrane integrity. This increases cell-membrane permeability, causing leakage of intracellular contents and bacterial death. It is bactericidal against most aerobic Gram-negative bacilli; organisms such as Proteus, Providencia, Serratia and most Gram-positives and anaerobes are intrinsically resistant.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to colistin or other polymyxins
Myasthenia gravis (risk of neuromuscular blockade, mainly with systemic exposure)
relative: Significant renal impairment (concern chiefly with systemic colistimethate, not oral sulphate)
Concomitant nephrotoxic or neurotoxic agents (if any systemic absorption)
monitor: Signs of neurotoxicity or nephrotoxicity if systemic absorption is possible (e.g., damaged gut mucosa)

preg: Data on colistin sulphate in pregnancy are limited. Systemic absorption from oral dosing is minimal, but use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the potential benefit justifies any potential risk; seek specialist advice.
lact: Use with caution during breastfeeding. Systemic absorption after oral dosing is minimal, limiting infant exposure, but data are limited; weigh the benefit of treatment against any theoretical risk.
renal: After oral dosing colistin sulphate is minimally absorbed, so systemic accumulation and dose adjustment are generally not needed for the gut-acting oral form. Caution is warranted if mucosal integrity is compromised (possible absorption) or if systemic polymyxin (colistimethate sodium) is used, where dose must be reduced in renal impairment because of dose-dependent nephrotoxicity.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is established; colistin is eliminated largely by the kidneys (systemic form) rather than hepatic metabolism. Oral sulphate acts locally in the gut with negligible systemic exposure.

major: Other nephrotoxic agents (aminoglycosides, amphotericin B) - additive renal toxicity if systemic absorption occurs
Neuromuscular blocking agents - potentiated neuromuscular blockade
Other neurotoxic agents - additive neurotoxicity with systemic exposure
moderate: Concomitant oral antibiotics altering gut flora - effect on decontamination regimens
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food. Oral colistin acts within the gut lumen.

serious: Nephrotoxicity (dose-dependent; chiefly with systemic colistimethate, rare with oral sulphate)
Neurotoxicity - paresthesia, dizziness, ataxia (chiefly with systemic exposure)
rare: Apnea (with high systemic exposure or neuromuscular blocker interaction)
emergency: Acute respiratory depression / apnea from neuromuscular blockade

monitoring: Renal function and neurological status if systemic absorption is possible or systemic polymyxin is used
Signs of superinfection or antibiotic-associated diarrhea
Therapeutic response of the targeted gut decontamination/infection
counsel: Take the full course exactly as prescribed, even if you feel better
This oral medicine works mainly inside the gut and is barely absorbed into the body
Report severe or persistent diarrhea, which could signal a gut infection
Report numbness, tingling, dizziness, muscle weakness or trouble breathing immediately
Tell your clinician about kidney problems or other antibiotics you take
Do not confuse this with injectable colistin (colistimethate) - they are not interchangeable
pk: Local gut action; acts within the intestinal lumen
Negligible systemic absorption after oral dosing (acts locally)
Minimal systemic exposure orally; systemic colistin half-life ~2-3 hours (colistimethate form)
Dosed three times daily for sustained luminal effect
Store per product labeling; reconstituted oral suspension refrigerated and used within stated period
pearls: Colistin SULPHATE is the oral/topical, locally acting form - distinct from colistimethate SODIUM, the parenteral/inhaled prodrug used for systemic and respiratory infection
Very poorly absorbed from the gut, so oral use is for bowel decontamination and GI infection, not systemic disease
Nephrotoxicity and neurotoxicity are the dose-limiting toxicities of systemic polymyxin therapy; oral sulphate carries low systemic risk unless gut mucosa is compromised
Polymyxins (systemic colistimethate) are last-resort agents for multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections - narrow therapeutic index; emerging plasmid-mediated mcr resistance
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue the regular three-times-daily schedule - do not double up. Complete the full prescribed course.
overdose: Oral overdose is unlikely to cause systemic toxicity because absorption is minimal, though gastrointestinal upset may occur. Significant systemic colistin overexposure (chiefly with the parenteral colistimethate form) can cause acute neuromuscular blockade with apnea, paresthesia, vertigo, and acute kidney injury. Management is supportive with airway/ventilatory support and renal monitoring; calcium salts may partially counter neuromuscular blockade, and hemodialysis/hemofiltration may aid removal in renal failure. Contact a poison control center.
